title: Validator and Repair Effects Under Shared-Initial-Candidate Semantics: A Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that measured the effect of a deterministic validator plus an at-most-one repair step when both baseline and guarded conditions begin from the identical sampled LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics). The preregistered study targeted retrieval-augmentation (RAG) poisoning attacks; the executed adapter contract disabled retrievals (retrieval_augmented_generation = false), so the realized estimand compares baseline single-shot validator outcomes on a shared sampled candidate against final guarded outcomes (validator ± permitted repair) on that same candidate. On N = 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) judged every sampled initial candidate valid (n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0), no repairs were applied, and baseline and guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rates were identical (1.0). Mapping actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run; we reconcile the archived artifacts, quantify the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0), document execution accounting, and provide artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-up preregistered experiments.

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed as building blocks for NetOps automation tasks such as intent→configuration translation, staged maintenance workflows, and zero-touch configuration [https://openalex.org/W4406137434, https://openalex.org/W4402742293, https://openalex.org/W4403635865]. Unconstrained generations may violate operational invariants (ordering, reachability, policy) and thus threaten network availability and safety. To mitigate this, tool-augmented architectures pair LLM generation with deterministic validators and bounded repairs (generate→validate→repair). Prior surveys and prototypes report both promise and residual risk, motivating controlled empirical studies of defended pipelines and adversarial failure modes [https://openalex.org/W4399629579, 10.20944/preprints202512.0913.v1].

We preregistered study candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to quantify whether targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) increases actionable-misconfiguration rates and whether deterministic defenses mitigate that effect. The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design (N = 250 tasks), a primary poison fraction of 0.30, and a single primary estimand: the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded minus baseline) under shared task instances. The executed adapter contract, however, set generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation = false (artifact-backed). Under these realized semantics baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled candidate; any paired difference can therefore only arise from the validator-triggered repair step. This paper reports the artifact-grounded outcomes under the executed semantics, reconciles the preregistration intent with execution artifacts, and draws conservative conclusions and recommendations grounded in the archived evidence.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys synthesize rapid adoption of LLMs for NetOps and emphasize the role of deterministic validators and tool augmentation to reduce hallucination and constraint violations [https://openalex.org/W4406137434, https://openalex.org/W4402742293]. Benchmarks and frameworks (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench) provide task banks and evaluation primitives but highlight construct-validity concerns for operational invariants (reachability, policy compliance) [https://openalex.org/W4399629579].

Adjacently, RAG and tool-augmented LLM pipelines in security operations and code translation have exposed concrete failure modes—hallucination, adversarially induced misinformation, and translation bugs—that motivate adversarial robustness studies for NetOps RAG pipelines [10.20944/preprints202512.0913.v1]. Proposals for calling deterministic verifiers or simulators (Batfish-style tools and similar validators) are prevalent in the literature; they show grounding benefits but raise latency and integration tradeoffs [https://openalex.org/W4389518608, doi:10.2139/ssrn.7317098]. The supplied literature thus supports: (1) the operational relevance of validators in LLM-driven NetOps, (2) the conceptual threat posed by poisoned retrievals in RAG pipelines, and (3) the need for artifact-grounded, preregistered empirical evaluation of defended architectures. Our contribution is an executed paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics with full artifact backing and explicit reconciliation of preregistration expectations and runtime contract.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 with primary hypothesis H1: poisoning at poison_fraction = 0.30 increases actionable-misconfiguration rates; and H2: deterministic retrieval filters mitigate poisoning. The preregistration artifact SHA‑256 (referenced in the execution manifest) is ebfbe67f56b5cfb4f0cdbf5a207c7cc095679771ab99515fa8d7d47b2f5e51e3. The design specified a paired confirmatory test across N_confirmatory = 250 tasks with preregistered exclusion rules (complete_pair_primary) and power calibrated to detect an absolute paired increase ≈ 0.045–0.06 assuming baseline actionable-misconfig ≈ 0.05.

Executed adapter contract and runtime semantics (artifact-backed). The archive shows the executed adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with declared_model_version "gpt-5-mini" recorded in execution/model_configuration.json (short form: sha a40e96e2...). Critical executed fields (artifact-backed) are: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task, reused across conditions), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, and retrieval_augmented_generation = false (no retrievals were performed). The model configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. We state these runtime facts explicitly to avoid misinterpretation: the run is not measuring effects of independent per-condition sampling or of RAG-based poisoning because both were disabled by the executed contract.

Task bank, validator and repair policy. Tasks: 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks generated deterministically (task_manifest archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl; representative reference-answer hash c8b7cf48...). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 produced per-episode VALID_CONFIGURATION judgments and deterministic validator traces archived under execution/scoring/*.json. Repair policy: at most one repair call per failing candidate; repair traces are null for all episodes because repairs were never applied. The scoring rule maps VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 to no actionable misconfiguration and actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION.

Sampling semantics, paired comparison, and statistical plan. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics each task produced a single sampled candidate during the shared_initial_generation stage; that identical candidate was assessed as baseline (validator outcome on sampled candidate) and guarded (final outcome after validator ± permitted repair). The primary estimand is the paired difference in actionable_misconfig indicator (guarded − baseline). The preregistered analysis used an exact McNemar two-sided test (α = 0.05) and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1. Missingness handling followed the preregistered complete_pair_primary rule; no pairs were excluded. The analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv) are archived and referenced in Results.

Deviations from conceptual preregistration. The preregistration conceptualized a RAG-based poisoning experiment. The executed contract disabled retrievals (retrieval_augmented_generation = false) and used shared_initial_candidate semantics; these execution facts are archived in execution/model_configuration.json (short: a40e96e2...) and execution/execution_manifest.json. Because the run adhered to the executed contract, the RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run. We record this execution-time realization here and reference the concrete artifacts that evidence the contract state. The archived analysis_results metadata contains deviations_from_preregistration = [] (immutable in the archive); the reconciliation in this manuscript makes the execution deviation machine-interpretable by citing the relevant artifacts and their archived short identifiers.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed). The run began 2026-08-31T21:04:12Z and completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56Z (execution manifest). Planned episodes = 500 (two conditions × 250 tasks); completed episodes = 500; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 250; cache_miss_count = 250; stage_counts show shared_initial_generation executed 250 times (no independent per-condition sampling). Model configuration is archived at execution/model_configuration.json (short id a40e96e2...), and raw results at execution/raw_results.jsonl (short id e3af400a9...).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed). The analysis contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; short id 1be58d82...) reports n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0; guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0. Under actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION this yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms and paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/missingness_summary.csv confirm no missing pairs or exclusions.

Representative episode diagnostics. Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json and -guarded.json; raw-response short id 2d39d60d...) show identical shared_initial_candidate content across arms and validator traces containing validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false. Repair_provider_trace entries are null because repairs were never invoked. deterministic_reconciliation.json records provider_call_audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 250 and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false, consistent with the single shared generation per task. These artifacts document the mechanistic reason for the null paired difference: the guard had no failing candidates to repair.

Power and assumption mismatch. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline actionable-misconfig ≈ 0.05. Observed baseline = 0.0 violates that assumption and renders the run insensitive to the originally preregistered poisoning effect sizes. We therefore treat the null paired difference as a precise artifact-grounded outcome for the executed estimand (shared_initial_candidate + deterministic validator) but not as evidence that guarded pipelines would be ineffective under RAG or independent-sampling regimes.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation limited to the executed estimand. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics and the deterministic validator used, every sampled candidate satisfied validation and repairs were never triggered; therefore the guarded pipeline could not alter paired outcomes. This result is an artifact‑grounded demonstration of a null effect of validator/repair when initial candidates are already valid and repairs are not invoked.

What the results do not show. The run did not exercise retrieval-augmented generation (retrieval_augmented_generation = false), did not permit independent per-condition sampling, used a single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini), and employed a single deterministic validator on synthetic tasks. Consequently the run cannot adjudicate the preregistered RAG-poisoning hypotheses nor generalize to production deployments, vendor-specific validators, or multi-model ensembles.

Construct, internal, and external validity threats (artifact-evidenced). Internal validity: provider-call and reconciliation artifacts (deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution manifest) confirm shared_initial_candidate semantics and one shared generation per task; this isolates validator/repair effects but precludes detecting effects that require per-condition sampling variability. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a specific rule set and reports parsed command counts and violation codes; validator completeness is therefore a construct-limitation—some vendor- or device-specific behaviors are not represented in the synthetic validator traces archived. External validity: synthetic task bank, single validator, and single model limit transferability to heterogeneous production topologies and multi-vendor environments. Conclusion validity: the homogeneous all-success outcome yields precise CIs reflecting the controlled corpus rather than operational heterogeneity; the original power assumptions do not hold for the observed baseline.

Operational implications and artifact-grounded recommendations. The archived run shows that when sampled candidates already satisfy a validator, guarded pipelines add zero marginal safety benefit for that corpus under shared_initial_candidate semantics. However, operational risk arises where generators produce invalid candidates or where adversarial retrievals bias generations; to measure mitigation under those threats requires follow-up preregistered runs that (1) enable retrieval_augmented_generation and controlled poison injection at predefined poison_fraction levels, (2) permit independent per-condition generation (generation_semantics != shared_initial_candidate) so baseline and guarded begin from independent samples, (3) broaden validators to vendor-aware simulators, and (4) test multiple sampling regimes and models. These concrete steps are consistent with the original preregistration and are supported by the archived artifact manifest as the natural next-stage experiments.

Reviewer-requested reconciliations. Reviewers requested explicit statements that the run used exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms and that temperature = null is not evidence of deterministic sampling. We have added those explicit statements in Methods and Disclosure and referenced model_configuration.json (short id a40e96e2...) and the preregistration SHA (ebfbe67f5...) so readers can machine-verify the execution-state artifacts. The archived analysis metadata showing deviations_from_preregistration = [] remains immutable; this manuscript reconciles that metadata by citing the execution artifacts that document the contract state and the resulting change in estimand.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (declared model: gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; retrieval disabled). All 250 shared sampled candidates passed deterministic validation (n11 = 250), no repairs were applied, and the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate is 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable; we documented and reconciled this execution-time realization against the archived preregistration and execution artifacts. Follow-up preregistered runs that enable controlled retrieval augmentation, independent per-condition sampling, broader validators, and multi-model ensembles are necessary to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as an execution-time realization documented in execution/model_configuration.json (short id a40e96e2...) and the execution manifest.

The stored scorer semantics required mapping to the preregistered estimand: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 corresponds to no actionable misconfiguration, hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This mapping was applied consistently in all reported analyses.

A single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
